title: Test a rewritten task with the old answer
statement: When an open task is rewritten, test its scoring with a fluent answer to the task it replaced, which must now fail, alongside good answers to the new one.
example: One unit rewrote three independent tasks that narration had already answered, and the rule now requires each replacement's scoring to reject a fluent answer to the old question.
detail: A final review of one unit found three independent tasks whose answers narrated commentary had already supplied, so a student could pass by repeating what the lesson said. Each was replaced by a task needing a new claim or new evidence, and each replacement's scoring examples list an answer to the superseded prompt among those to reject. The course then made it a rule to give every replacement task separate positive and negative scoring examples, including a fluent response to the superseded question that must now fail.

evidence.quote: It found three independent tasks whose answers had already been supplied by narrated commentary.
Also use separate positive and negative scoring examples for the replacement task, including a fluent response to the superseded question that must now fail.
Earlier reading-b explicitly supplies a long basket search as a way to show doubt.
